source.title: On the Validity of Modeling SGD with Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs)
source.authors: Zhiyuan Li; Sadhika Malladi; Sanjeev Arora

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and figure descriptions.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own results that refine the claim: test accuracy is similar for SGD and covariance-matched Gaussian-noise descent, while SDE approximation and linear scaling can fail in specified settings. It does not test most claim versions directly.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper’s own CIFAR-10 SGD-versus-GD/NGD test-accuracy comparisons and SVAG outcomes that bear on V1. LSR error plots are figure-based and concern batch-size scaling; their reported result is summarized in the paper’s text, while this claim’s V5 concerns a separate fixed-epoch generalization-gap claim. Cited prior-work results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The fixed-epoch batch-size sweeps in Figures 2 and 15–17 test V5: held-out error rises beyond workload-dependent batch sizes despite linear learning-rate scaling. The SGD/GD/NGD comparisons do not test V1 because they contain no random-label experiment.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors introduce SVAG, prove its convergence to the canonical order-1 SDE under stated assumptions, and find that this SDE captures SGD behavior in many common settings. They derive and experimentally evaluate a necessary condition for SDE approximation and linear scaling, while reporting exceptions. Covariance-matched NGD also closely matches SGD in their CIFAR-10 experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests SDE approximations and covariance-matched noisy gradient descent, not random-label memorization or the claim’s paired natural-label versus random-label protocol. For V1, it reports CIFAR-10 natural-label results under SGD, GD and NGD.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported SGD/NGD comparison depends on model, learning rate, batch size, normalization choice and data augmentation. The paper states SDE approximation fails in certain large-batch/linear-scaling settings; GroupNorm on CIFAR-100 is also identified as an exception.

fits_no_version.finding: Covariance-matched NGD closely matches SGD test accuracy, while full-gradient GD performs worse in the reported CIFAR-10 experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Replacing SGD noise with Gaussian noise of matching covariance can preserve held-out performance in these vision settings.

fits_no_version.finding: SVAG approximates SGD in many settings but diverges in specified large-batch settings and with GroupNorm on CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The canonical SDE can capture SGD training and generalization trajectories in many settings, with identifiable exceptions.

record.problems: No random-label experiment, so this paper does not establish that a network fitting random labels also generalizes on natural labels. Accuracy values are reported in figure descriptions without error bars or statistical uncertainty. The paper notes that its SVAG theory does not cover random-shuffling sampling, although its experiments use it.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the extracted V1 results. Figure 2 and Figures 15–17 include batch-size-dependent train/test error plots for the paper’s LSR/SDE question, not the fixed-epoch generalization-gap claim in V5; exact plotted values are figure-only, so they are not reconstructed here. Other SVAG curves across architectures and settings are described qualitatively in Figures 7–14, but do not directly measure the V1 random-label behavior.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, random-label held-out accuracy, and coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.

Language models; recovery through longer training, warmup, or changes to normalization and regularization. Normalization settings are studied, but the text does not establish a controlled recovery intervention.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: V5 needs rows for final held-out error across batch sizes at fixed epoch budgets with linearly scaled learning rates. These sweeps are acknowledged in rows_left_out, but their exclusion incorrectly leaves V5 marked untested. Record readable values or explicit qualitative outcomes without reconstructing unavailable numerical points.
missing.locator: Figure 2; Appendix F.2, Figures 15–17. CIFAR experiments use 300 epochs; the SVHN sweep uses 120 epochs.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Generic evidence of natural-label generalization cannot support V1 without its memorization comparison. The noise-to-signal diagnostic is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure. Exact critical batch sizes and individual plotted errors are not reliably recoverable from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting random labels, chance-level random-label accuracy, or the specified Inception, AlexNet, and MLP settings.

rows.subject: GD
rows.operation_detail: Trained with infinitesimal-LR gradient descent; test accuracy compared with SGD and NGD.
rows.note: Lower test accuracy than finite-LR SGD and covariance-matched NGD; comparison is relevant to the claim’s contrast between training procedures, but it does not evaluate random-label memorization.
rows.check: Natural-label accuracy alone does not test V1's coexistence claim. Figure 19 reports 76.5%; Figure 3 reports a separate 75.5% result. The operation incorrectly describes infinitesimal learning rate: Figure 19 specifies finite LR 0.8 for all three methods. Batch size 125 describes the SGD comparator.

rows.subject: SGD
rows.operation_detail: Standard stochastic gradient descent on natural labels; test accuracy reported alongside GD and NGD.
rows.note: Natural-label test accuracy under SGD; random-label fitting and random-label test performance are not measured.
rows.check: The 86.9% natural-label accuracy is correctly reported but does not measure random-label fitting or its coexistence with generalization.

rows.subject: NGD
rows.operation_detail: Noisy gradient descent using Gaussian noise matched to SGD covariance.
rows.note: Authors report SGD and NGD have close train and test curves; this comparator is a Gaussian-noise method, not the random-label control in V1.
rows.check: The 86.8% versus 86.9% comparison tests covariance-matched Gaussian noise, not any listed version.

rows.subject: NGD
rows.operation_detail: Noisy gradient descent using Gaussian noise matched to SGD covariance.
rows.note: Authors report close train and test curves for covariance-matched NGD and SGD.
rows.check: The 82.5% versus 82.3% comparison tests NGD versus SGD at the same batch setting. It does not test V1 or establish a fixed-epoch batch-size comparison for V5.

rows.subject: GD

rows.check: The 75.5% value is correctly reported in Figure 3 but does not test a listed version. Batch size 125 describes the SGD comparator.

relationships.condition: Batch sizes beyond the workload-dependent scaling threshold in the fixed-epoch CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN sweeps
relationships.reason: Text and Figures 2 and 15–17 report large-batch scaling failure, defined as final test error exceeding the best achieved error by more than 20%, despite proportional learning-rate scaling. This verdict rests on the text and figures; no existing row captures these sweeps.
relationships.display_finding: Final test error increased beyond batch-size thresholds despite proportional learning-rate scaling, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
